title: Russia and NATO: missiles, plots and closed borders on Europe's eastern edge
dek: Russian missiles have landed in Poland, Estonia is closing its border, Denmark has expelled a Russian diplomat, and Ukraine's war is reaching ships far from the front.
seoTitle: Russia and NATO's eastern flank: timeline
bigLabel: Kh-101 cruise missiles that came down in south-east Poland during a Russian attack on Ukraine on 20 November, per Polish prosecutors. No one was hurt.

glance.what: A run of incidents linked to Russia has hit NATO and EU countries. Russian missiles came down in Poland in July and again on 20 November. Estonia blames Russian military intelligence for an arson attempt and is closing its road border with Russia. Denmark expelled Russia's defence attaché over an alleged murder plot. Ukraine says it hit a Russian warship in a Libyan port.
glance.why: NATO's 32 members have promised to treat an attack on one as an attack on all. Each incident tests how the alliance responds without being drawn into the war. Border closures, air-raid alerts and expulsions also affect travel and trade in the region.
glance.next: Estonia closes its three road crossings with Russia from 1 December. NATO has sent an early-warning radar plane (AWACS) to Poland and says Russia "bears full responsibility" for the missiles. A Russian drone briefly entered Polish airspace on 23 November and was not shot down. Poland is again asking the US for permanent troops. Russia says Estonia is "on the verge of triggering open war"; Estonia denies Russia's claims.

forYou: For most readers in India nothing changes directly. A wider conflict in Europe could push up oil and gas prices and disrupt flights over the region; Estonia's border closure affects travellers between the Baltics and Russia.

upcoming.label: 1 Dec
upcoming.text: Estonia closes its road border crossings with Russia, for at least six months

next: Estonia's border closure on 1 December; whether NATO strengthens air defence over Poland; Russia's response to Estonia.

events.title: Poland calls emergency NATO talks after Russian drones enter its airspace
events.summary: Several Russian drones crossed into Poland during an attack on Ukraine. Polish and Dutch fighter jets shot some of them down. Poland invoked Article 4 of NATO's treaty, which lets a member call emergency talks with allies when it feels threatened.

events.title: Russian missile explodes in a field in eastern Poland
events.summary: A missile came down in eastern Poland during a Russian attack on western Ukraine, leaving a crater about 10 metres wide. No one was hurt. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it was likely a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile. NATO scrambled fighter jets, and Secretary General Mark Rutte called it "yet another reckless act by Russia".

events.title: Estonia blames Russian military intelligence for an arson attempt and moves to close its border
events.summary: Estonia's Internal Security Service said Russia's military intelligence (GRU) ordered an attempted arson attack on a drone maker near Tallinn on 14 November, the second such attempt on a defence company since August. Eight Latvian citizens were detained. On 15 November the government moved to close its three road crossings with Russia, at Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula, from 1 December. Russia denies involvement.

events.title: Three Russian cruise missiles come down in south-east Poland
events.summary: Three objects fell in south-east Poland during a large Russian attack on Ukraine. Polish prosecutors in Lublin said on 22 November that all three were Kh-101 cruise missiles, per Notes from Poland. They were in Polish airspace for about three minutes, and no one was hurt. Prime Minister Tusk called it an apparent "intentional provocation", timed to a military exercise in Poland. NATO's Rutte would not say whether it was deliberate. Russia had not commented.
events.differs: Early reports quoting Poland's defence minister (Al Jazeera, 21 November) described two missiles and a jet-powered drone; prosecutors later said all three were missiles.

events.title: Denmark expels Russia's defence attaché over an alleged plot to kill a Ukrainian-American rapper
events.summary: Denmark's intelligence service (PET) said Russian intelligence planned to have a Ukrainian-American rapper killed at a concert near Copenhagen, using a banned Danish gang. Two Danish men were charged with attempted murder; both reportedly deny it. Denmark gave Russia's defence attaché seven days to leave. Russia's embassy called the expulsion "vengeful" and said Denmark had shown no evidence.

events.title: Drones hit Russian ships in the Gulf of Finland and in a Libyan port
events.summary: On 21 November drones hit the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland; all 16 crew were evacuated, per Al Jazeera. Kyiv has not claimed that attack. On 22 November Ukrainian sea drones hit the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi, Libya, President Zelenskyy said the next day, about 2,400 km from the front line. Libya's eastern government asked the UN for an investigation.
events.status: Stated · Zelenskyy (Libya); Reported · Al Jazeera (Sparta II)
events.differs: Zelenskyy says the Merkury sank; two Libyan officials told AP it was badly damaged, not sunk.

events.title: NATO sends a radar plane to Poland; Russia warns Estonia of 'open war'
events.summary: NATO ambassadors met in Brussels, and NATO's top military commander ordered an AWACS early-warning radar plane to Poland. NATO said Russia "bears full responsibility" for the missiles. Poland did not formally ask for Article 4 talks this time. The same day Russia's foreign ministry summoned Estonia's acting envoy in Moscow and said Estonia was "on the verge of triggering open war". Estonia denied letting Ukraine use its airspace.
events.status: Confirmed · NATO; Stated · Russian foreign ministry

sources.name: Reuters World News Summary via Devdiscourse

events.title: Russian drone briefly enters Polish airspace; Poland says a NATO jet was cleared to fire on the 20 November missile
events.summary: Late on 23 November a Russian drone "briefly violated Polish airspace" during attacks on western Ukraine, Poland's military said. Permission to shoot it down was given, but it was not fired on after it turned east, because of the risk to people on the ground, per ABC News. It flew over Dorohusk, a border town with a major rail and freight crossing, for several minutes. A deputy defence minister said Poland assumes it was deliberate; Russia's ambassador said no convincing evidence has been shown. Separately, Poland's operational commander, Lt Gen Ireneusz Nowak, said a Swedish Gripen jet under NATO command was cleared to fire at a Russian cruise missile on 20 November, but bad weather stopped the pilot finding it, per Fox News. Poland has again asked the US for permanent troops. Estonia's foreign minister wrote that closing the border "will limit opportunities for hostile intelligence activities", per TIME.
events.status: Confirmed · Polish military; Stated · Lt Gen Nowak (NATO jet)
